partial_progress.details: Phase 8 of 11 (One-Process-Per-File Shellcheck Parallelization) complete and committed cleanly (290bf659b). lint-shellcheck.sh now dispatches one shellcheck process per file via a wait -n-bounded worker pool (sc_run_one), mirroring run-all.sh's own run_one() shape, capped by SHELLCHECK_JOBS (default 8, env-overridable, chosen from a fresh P=1/4/8/12 re-run of the worker-count experiment on the real 387-file corpus, never a bare nproc). Both the default git-ls-files corpus scan and the explicit-path/find-based fixture path share the same pool. Measured before/after (the phase's entire purpose): SHELLCHECK_JOBS=1 vs default across three independent same-host A/B pairs showed 76778ms->39455ms, 136376ms->45475ms, and the raw worker-count exploration's 75778ms->42006ms/38355ms -- a real 1.8x-3x win (better than the research's budgeted 1.3-1.8x), not merely configured-but-unmeasured. Every pair produced 0 findings on both sides (finding-SET equivalence, not just timing). Finding-set equivalence additionally proven against the PRE-CHANGE original script via a throwaway git worktree: byte-identical output on the real corpus and on a seeded SC2155 fixture. Gate 22 via the full verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 22 --findings --quiet <repo-root> wrapper passed clean (50s) against the source store. A new acceptance suite, test-lint-shellcheck-parallel.sh (9 cases: real-corpus equivalence+ratio-gate, seeded-violation equivalence, cross-worker-count determinism, SHELLCHECK_JOBS validation), registered in run-all.sh's LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES, passed both standalone and via run-all.sh --only. Broader regression net re-run clean: test-deploy-baseline-lib.sh, test-orchestrate-batch-gate.sh, test-run-all-selection.sh, test-gate-registry-resolution.sh, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh, test-lint-shellcheck.sh -- 6/6 via one run-all.sh --jobs auto invocation (caveat: test-lint-shellcheck.sh itself resolves deploy-tree-first, so that one result exercised the stale deployed copy, not this phase's source-store change; every other check in this list exercised the source-store path directly). SEQUENCING DEVIATION, disclosed not silently fixed: the phase-8 handoff markdown was written AFTER the phase-closing commit instead of before it, so it is NOT included in that commit (290bf659b) as the single-commit-per-phase rule requires. No second, provenance-only commit was created to correct this (that would violate the same rule from the other direction, and a HEAD-moving amend is unsafe with other writers live in this repo) -- the handoff file sits uncommitted in the tree pending Phase 9's own first commit or this orchestration cycle's postflight commit. Pausing at this clean phase boundary per the coordinator's explicit instruction to finalize now; Phase 9 (Shared Corpus Enumeration) depends on Phase 7 (complete) and can start cleanly, but its own Scope Hypothesis already flags that the dispatch's 'six lints share one git ls-files list' framing is confirmed wrong by the research and must be re-derived at implementation time.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a repeatable CI/acceptance test that compares wall-clock timing between two code paths (e.g. parallel vs sequential) on a shared, multi-tenant dev host, never assert an absolute-ms threshold -- ambient contention from unrelated concurrent processes can inflate both legs by 2-3x and make a correct implementation fail the gate. Instead measure both legs back-to-back in the SAME run and assert a RELATIVE ratio (e.g. 'parallel <= 80% of forced-sequential'), sized with real margin over the clean-host measurement. This survived a live ambient-load spike (one leg's absolute time varied from 76s to 136s across runs on the same unchanged code) while still catching a genuine regression back to no-parallelism. Precedent for the pattern already existed in this codebase (test-run-all-parallel.sh's prior fix for an identical flake class); reuse it rather than re-deriving per new parallel feature.

To verify a source-store script change's finding-set is unchanged from its pre-change behavior, when the deployed copy is stale (not yet redeployed) and a sibling fixture-test file resolves its subject deploy-tree-first, do not trust that test's PASS as evidence -- it is silently exercising the OLD deployed copy. Instead, create a throwaway `git worktree add --detach HEAD <path>` to get a clean checkout of the pre-change tree, invoke the ORIGINAL script directly from within it (so its own relative sourcing of sibling lib files still resolves), and diff its output against the new script's output on the same real corpus and a seeded-violation fixture. Clean up with `git worktree remove <path> --force` when done. This gives true byte-for-byte before/after equivalence evidence independent of deploy state.
